To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HLAD-NAD+-XyHP ternary complex is a substrate for HLAD, which converts the coenzyme into an inactive form, and the enzyme itself is inhibited by the reaction product.
the hydroperoxides of aromatic alcohols inhibit HLAD activity and are degraded by the enzyme to the alcohols and the non-inhibitory oxidation products.

Horse liver alcohol dehydro-genase, an enzyme that catalyzes oxidation of primary alcohols to the corresponding aldehydes, also catalyzes the oxidation of hydroperoxides, such as p-methylben-zyl hydroperoxide, to non-inhibiting reaction products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inhibition of HLAD by XyHP.
the inhibition and degradation of HLAD by hydrogen peroxide and p-methylbenzylic hydroperoxide.
a novel type of HLAD inhibition and with the HLAD-catalysed degradation of a hydroperoxide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
XyHP is a pseudo-substrate and a transient inhibitor of HLAD.
XyHP is not an inhibitor, but a substrate, and HLAD is an enzyme which catalyses the degradation of Xyhp, and the NAD+ derivative formed in this reaction is a product.
the hydroperoxide XyHP behaves both as a substrate and an inhibitor for HLAD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
XyHP is a pseudo-substrate inhibitor of HLAD.
the inhibition of the HLAD-NAD+-XyHP complex is a consequence of the degradation of XyH2O2 by HLAD to non-inhibiting product(s) while the NAD+, originally bound to HLAD, is converted to NADX.
the HLAD-NAD+-hydroperoxide complex is an enzyme-substrate complex which is catalytically active in the degradation of the hydroperoxide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HLAD-NAD+-XyHP complex is a good model system for studying the mechanism of HLAD inhibition by hydrogen peroxide.
HLAD can be used as a tool for the study of the chemistry of organic hydroperoxides.
HLAD has an intrinsic capacity for the degradation of hydroperoxides.
